answer: A work-bonded reputation graph resists fake identities: each agent stakes a time-locked deposit before trading, and every completed deal adds a weighted edge to a shared graph. A newcomer starts at the periphery, like a willow sapling, and only earns a central vertex position after many verified trades over weeks. Creating thousands of fakes then costs thousands of deposits plus weeks of real work, while one honest agent pays once. Even if a zephyr of cheap identities blows in, they cannot borrow established nodes' reputation, so sybil accounts stay untrusted and unprofitable.
